Inserts a WebGL pass between 2D draws. (draws the preceding 2D batch, clears depth, then callback, and restoreRenderState when done)
- callback receives the WebGL2 context and may freely change the program, vertex array, viewport, blending, depth and face culling. (the stencil clip stays applied, and the stencil state is not restored, so do not change it)
- If callback throws, the state is restored and the error is rethrown.
- Even when WebGL is used through the same context outside this function, the next 2D draw compares the program, vertex array, texture units, blending, depth, face culling, scissor and viewport against the state cache and sets them again.
  Two promises remain. 2D draws into the framebuffer bound now, so if the game bound its own framebuffer it puts back the one it found, and it does not change the stencil state.

2D 물리 월드.\n- 초안: 0.4.0 뒤 기능, API 가 바뀔 수:
2D physics world.
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change.
- Holds rigid bodies (static, kinematic, dynamic), shapes (circle, capsule, segment, convex polygon, chain) and joints (distance, revolute, weld, wheel), and runs steps.
  The features are based on Box2D 3 (Erin Catto) and Unity 2D physics (Rigidbody2D, Collider2D).
- The broad phase is a dynamic AABB tree (DynamicTree), the narrow phase is separating axes and edge clipping, and the solver is a soft step (substeps, warm starting, soft constraints, relaxation, restitution),
  grouping touching bodies into islands and putting a whole island to sleep when it stays still.
- Determinism: all math is f64 and the trigonometric functions are hand-written. Creating in the same order and calling the same step gives results identical to the bit with the same world in the Rust vanilla-engine.
- step(timeStep, subStepCount) takes one step of that time, and advance(timeDelta) accumulates and runs fixed steps (FixedStepper) and returns the draw interpolation fraction.
- Events (contact begin and end, sensor enter and exit) are gathered fresh on every step and can be read until the next step.
- Not there yet: continuous collision (TOI, which keeps fast bullets from tunneling through thin walls), one-sided chains, prismatic, motor and mouse joints, changing body types, multithreading.
2D 물리의 결정론 수학.\n- 초안: 0.4.0 뒤 기능, API 가:
Deterministic math for 2D physics.
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change.
- Builds cosine, sine and arctangent from only addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and square root. (all operations IEEE 754 requires to be correctly rounded)
  The browser's Math.sin and Rust's f64::sin differ in the last digits across operating systems and engines, so the physics of the two engines diverge on the same input.
  Box2D wrote b2ComputeCosSin and b2Atan2 itself for the same reason. (box2d.org/posts/2024/08/determinism)
- Same math in the same order as experimental::physics2d::PhysicsMath2D of the Rust vanilla-engine, so the results of the two engines match to the bit.

2D 뼈대 애니메이션의 곡선, 시간줄, 자세, 클립.\n- 초안: 0.4:
Curves, timelines, poses and clips of 2D skeletal animation.
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change.
- A curve is the interpolation from each key to the next. There are three: linear, stepped, and cubic Bezier ([x1, y1, x2, y2] like CSS cubic-bezier, end points (0, 0), (1, 1)).
- Bone timeline values are relative to the setup pose. Rotation, translation and shear are added and scale is multiplied. (same form as Spine and DragonBones)
- Slot colors are used as is, attachments and draw order are stepped, and events fire once at their time.
- A pose (Skeleton2DPose) is an array holding only bone local values and slot states. Clips write values into poses, and blending blends poses together.

2D skeleton animator component. (attached to a node to run and draw a skeleton)
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change.
- Holds a Skeleton2D (pose) and a Skeleton2DAnimationState (tracks), advances time and writes the pose in tick, and computes world matrices and IK and draws in draw.
  Since it computes in draw, bones the scene's tick moved after the component tick (like IK targets) also apply in that frame.
- Images are found by the frame names of attachments. setAtlas finds and stores the frames of all skins from an engine SpriteAtlas, and setFrame can add them one at a time.
- For each slot in draw order, triangles are written into the Graphic vertex slots (getVertexData, x, y, u, v) and drawn with drawVertices. The slot color is multiplied into the image.
  Slots with images on the same page are drawn at once by the engine's batching. Graphic was not modified.
- The skeleton origin is the node's pivot position. (the node position if the content size is 0)
- It is separate from SpriteAnimator (frame animation). That one changes the Sprite image of the same node; this one draws by itself.
- With gizmos on (setGizmoVisible), bones are drawn as lines.

- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change.
- Bone local values (translation, rotation, scale, shear) are written by clips or code. updateWorldTransform computes the world matrices from the parents down and applies IK.
- IK does not change local values, only the 'applied rotation' (getAppliedRotation). The next computation starts again from the local values, so nothing accumulates.
- One-bone IK rotates the bone so its x axis faces the target. Two-bone IK rotates the parent by the law of cosines to place the elbow and rotates the child to face the target.
  If out of reach, it straightens. It blends with the original rotation by the mix (mix). If the grandparent bone is flipped (negative determinant), the bend direction is flipped. (same as DragonBones)
- The data (Skeleton2DData) is the setup pose shared by instances, so it is frozen when an instance is built. After that, the data setters and add methods throw. (The Rust edition shares it through Rc, which blocks &mut)

- Coordinates have y growing downward like the engine. Rotation and shear are in degrees, and positive is clockwise on screen.
- Bone local matrix: x axis = (cos(rotation + shear x), sin(rotation + shear x)) x scale x, y axis = (-sin(rotation + shear y), cos(rotation + shear y)) x scale y.

3D 모형 짓기. (기본 도형을 코드로 지어 꼭짓점 배열 하나에 담음)\:
Builds 3D models. (builds primitive shapes in code and puts them into one vertex array)

Builds vertex arrays for drawing toon 3D (clay-like single-color material and outline). Comes from the board 3D of webgame-rimminer. (same form as three.js primitive geometries)
  - Shapes are built in their own coordinates with the center at the origin. When adding a part, position, rotation and scale are multiplied in and it is put into one chunk.
  - One vertex is position 3, normal 3, color 3 (sRGB), material 2 (glow strength, unlit), pattern 4 (pattern number, pattern color). The meaning of pattern number and color is decided by the drawing shader. (0 means no pattern)
  - Texture coordinates (UV) are stored separately, 2 per vertex, in uvData outside the vertex array. If even one vertex has UV given, the rest are filled with 0. (the shape's uvs, addTriangles' uvs)
    (0, 0) is the top left of the image. (same as glTF) Boxes are 0 ~ 1 per face, spheres are 0 ~ 1 by longitude and latitude.

Builds the vertex array used to draw toon 3D (single-color clay-like material with outlines). It came from the in-board 3D of webgame-rimminer. (Same form as the three.js basic geometries)
  - Shapes are built in their own coordinates with the center at the origin. When a part is added, position, rotation and scale are multiplied in and it is put into one lump.
  - One vertex is position 3, normal 3, color 3 (sRGB), material 2 (glow strength, unlit), pattern 4 (pattern number, pattern color). The meaning of the pattern number and color is decided by the shader that draws it. (0 means no pattern)
  - Texture coordinates (UV) are stored separately, 2 per vertex, in uvData outside the vertex array. If even one vertex was given a UV, the rest are filled with 0. (uvs of a shape, uvs of addTriangles)

    (0, 0) is the top left of the image. (Same as glTF) A box is 0 ~ 1 per face, a sphere is 0 ~ 1 by longitude and latitude.

  - The outline is a slightly enlarged copy of the part. Since only its back faces are drawn, it is stored separately. (inverted hull)

Characters shared by several fonts, such as Han characters, are drawn by the font registered later. The selected language's font group is registered right before Latin (second from the end)
so that Japanese gets Japanese-font Han characters and Traditional Chinese gets Traditional-font ones. Latin is always last, so digits and Latin letters use the Latin font in every language.
Subsets under one font name must all declare the same weight to be selected together by character range. (because the weight is chosen first and only subsets of that weight are considered)
So every subset is registered with only the two weights in configureUiFont's weights (initially 500, 700). Variable-weight subsets are registered twice (500 and 700), and 400-only subsets as 500.
When the screen requests 400, the 500 subset draws, and for 600 the 700 subset draws.
The canvas does not wait for subsets not yet downloaded and draws with another font, so subsets for the characters to be drawn are fetched in advance. (loadUiFontText)
When a subset is downloaded, the engine (EngineConfiguration.rebakeTextOnFontLoad) discards and rebakes only the text images baked with that subset's characters.
The font lists are split per group. (fonts.json is the index, fonts-<group>.json holds that group's subsets)
At first only the lists for the selected language and Latin are fetched, and the rest (language names in the language window, other scripts such as person names) are fetched a little after play starts.
Initial subsets are waited for only up to configureUiFont's waitMilliseconds, after which play starts first and text is rebaked as subsets arrive. (shorter first load)
Paths are written as literal strings so the build's cache busting can add fingerprints. (subset fingerprints are added to the lists by the build)

UI 노드.\n- 기존 WorldNode 계열과 다른 별도 노선의 UI:
UI node.
- A UI node on a separate track from the existing WorldNode family.
- The area is defined by 8 solver variables (left / right / top / bottom / width / height
  + derived centerX / centerY), and the user places constraints on the LayoutSolver
  to determine those values.
- This class holds the variables and the essential constraints (right == left + width, bottom == top
  + height, centerX == left + width/2, centerY == top + height/2), and registers these 4
  automatically.
- User constraints are registered with addConstraint(constraint).
- The solver is attached with setSolver(solver). When operating the whole tree together, set it only on the root UINode
  and the caller manages it so that children receive the same instance through setSolver.
- intrinsicContentSize / contentHuggingPriority / contentCompressionResistancePriority
  follow the same idea as UIKit's APIs of the same name. Subclasses override getIntrinsicContentSize.
- layoutMargins / layoutMarginsGuide follow the same idea as UIKit's UIView.layoutMargins /
  layoutMarginsGuide. The guide, in the form of a child UINode, is exposed lazily.
UI 라벨.\n- 표시 전용. 입력을 받지 않으므로 UIView 를 상속:
UI label.
- Display only. Inherits UIView since it takes no input.
- When attached to a node, attaches both the Text and RichText components internally.
  (RichText inherits Text, so the component add order is fixed as Text → RichText)
- The default mode is plain text. Calling useRichText(true) enables RichText so that
  markup such as <b> / <i> / <u> / <s> / <color=...> / <size=N> is interpreted.
- All text / font / style setters are synced to both Text / RichText.
  (so the text is kept when the mode toggles)
- On setText, calls the host node's invalidateIntrinsicContentSize automatically.

UI scale.
- The fixed side of the view (height for portrait, width for landscape) always has the same length, so on a small screen (a portal's PC iframe, etc.)
  one view unit becomes much smaller than 1 CSS pixel on screen and text becomes unreadable. In that case it computes a scale that enlarges only the UI layer on screen. (the game's graphics stay as they are)
- If one unit is smaller than minimumCssScale CSS pixels, it enlarges by that much. (1 ~ maximumScale)
  - On a short screen, it does not enlarge so far that the enlarged UI layer's height falls below minimumLayerHeight. (so the top and bottom UI do not cover the screen in phone landscape, 0 means not checked)
  - On a portrait screen (width at most portraitRatio times the height), it enlarges without an upper limit so that one unit becomes minimumCssScale CSS pixels.
- Usage: const uiScale = UIScale.read(viewWidth, viewHeight); layerNode.setLocalScale(Vector2.create(uiScale, uiScale));
  UIWindowLayer enlarges windows by this scale.

UI 씬.\n- Scene 을 직접 상속받는 독립 베이스 씬.\n- Ga:
UI scene.
- Standalone base scene that directly inherits Scene.
- Has its own common infrastructure identical to GameScene (developer tools / touch routing / loading screen /
  env() safe-area insets / automatic viewSize detection / canvas background clear).
- Has its own LayoutSolver instance. Calls updateVariables automatically every tick.
- Has its own screen guide UINode (screenNode). Fixed at top-left (0, 0), with width/height
  registered as edit variables and updated via suggestValue on resize.
  (same idea as UIKit's UIWindow.bounds)
- Has a separate safeAreaLayoutGuide UINode. Represents the area inset from screenNode by
  safeAreaInsets. (same idea as UIKit's UIView.safeAreaLayoutGuide)
  In the layout() phase, env() insets are automatically applied to setSafeAreaInsets.
- UINodes added to the tree are automatically attached to the solver on tick.

고정 걸음.\n- 프레임 간격이 들쭉날쭉해도 규칙(물리, 판의 흐름)은:
Fixed step.
- Even if frame intervals are uneven, rules (physics, round flow) always run at the same step (stepSeconds).
- advance(timeDelta, stepFunction) accumulates the received time and calls stepFunction(stepSeconds) each time a full step accumulates.
  The returned value is the remaining fraction (0 ~ 1). Drawing by blending the previous step and the current step by this fraction keeps the steps from jittering against the screen refresh rate.
- Runs at most maximumStepsPerFrame steps per frame. If time still remains after that many, the remaining time is discarded.
  (So a slow device does not get even slower by running the backlog all at once after a stall)
- If stepFunction returns false, this frame's steps stop there and the remaining time stays accumulated. (For holding briefly, as in meetings or cutscenes)

- It is multiplied by the world size of one texel (light matrix width / resolution), so the same amount applies when the extent or resolution changes. (the same units as Depth Bias and Normal Bias in Unity URP)
- Depth bias pulls the compared depth toward the light. Normal bias pushes the receiving point along the surface normal before reading. Both are multiplied by the 1.5 texel radius of the 3x3 PCF.
- ToonRenderer adds a slope-scaled bias on top (grows as the light grazes the surface, 2.5 texels x slope, slope clamped at 10).
- Lower values keep shadows attached but invite self-shadow acne. Higher values remove acne but make shadows look detached (peter panning).

Shadow atlas. (Stores real-time shadows of point lights and spotlights as tiles in one depth texture)
- Same form as the additional light shadow atlas of Unity URP. A spotlight is drawn into one perspective shadow map tile, a point light draws the six cube faces into six tiles (90 degree perspective per face).
- updateLights(light list) picks lights with castsShadow true up to SHADOW_ATLAS_MAXIMUM_LIGHTS, divides the tiles and computes view and projection per tile.
  Lights have the form of ToonLightSet.setPointLights. { position, direction (spotlight if present), outerConeAngle, range (far distance, 30 if 0), shadowNear (near distance, default 0.05), castsShadow }
  The order in the list (lightIndex) is noted so ToonRenderer attaches this shadow to that point light. (The atlas is built from the point light list of the default light set)
- Tile size is decided the same as the Unity URP defaults. Each tile asks for tileResolution (default 1024, the default of the URP additional light shadow resolution tier High, and High is the default tier of a light),
  and if they do not all fit in the atlas (default 2048, the URP default), the tile side is halved until they all fit. (Doubling shadowSlicesScaleFactor of URP)
  Tiles are placed in order on a grid of gridSize per side. (gridSize = floor(resolution / tile side)) One point light (six tiles) gives 512, one spotlight gives 1024.
- Drawing: beginRender() clears the target, then per tile beginTile(tile number) sets the viewport to that tile and depth is drawn with getTile(tile number).viewProjectionMatrix. (ToonRenderer.beginShadowAtlasPass and setShadowAtlasTile do this sequence)
- Receiving: the shader picks the point light face from the direction from the light position to the surface (largest axis), computes the position and depth inside the tile from the forward, up and right basis and the near and far distances, and compares with 3x3 PCF.
  The receiving position is pushed toward the normal by (1 + 3 x (1 - dot(N, L))) tile texels at that distance before comparing. (Larger the more the surface is slanted to the light, prevents saw-toothed shadow acne at the light and shade boundary)

- Laying a shadow with two text nodes (the same text in black below, the text on top) makes the two show through separately, so when the node is faded the shadow beneath shows through the faded text.
  This component bakes the look of the text placed over the shadow into one canvas and draws that single sheet, so the node's opacity applies to the text and shadow as one sheet.

- Rebakes when the draw scale (device DPR, view scale), text, style or node width changes, or when a new web font chunk is downloaded.
- The shadow can be painted with the canvas shadow so that it blurs. The baked canvas edge is widened by the blur amount.
- Italic, underline, strikethrough (setItalic, setUnderline, setStrikethrough): the line position and thickness are the same as Text's middle baseline, and the lines are baked together with the text so the shadow lies beneath them too.

노드 레이아웃.\n- 지역 변수 없이 노드 계층 구조를 선언적으로 구성하:
Node layout.
- A fluent builder that declaratively composes the node hierarchy without local variables.
- A structure similar to Unreal Slate / Flutter widgets.
- Specifies all positions/sizes with number pairs (x, y) without Vector2.
- Specifies the node type with create(nodeClass). (default: WorldNode)

Example:
  const panel = NodeLayout.create(WorldNode)
      .pivot(Pivot.middleCenter)
      .contentSize(680, 900)
      .component(Paint, (c) => { c.setColor(new Color(0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 1)); })
      .children(
          NodeLayout.create(WorldNode)
              .contentSize(120, 70)
              .component(Text, (c) => { c.setText("OK"); })
      )
      .build();

누르는 자리 넓히기.\n- 보이는 단추는 그대로 두고, 단추 바로 뒤 형:
Expands the press area.
- Keeps the visible button as is, and places a transparent press area as the sibling right behind the button to widen its width and height to at least the minimum size. (easier to press with a finger)
- The node later in draw order receives the press, so presses on the button are received by the button and only the widened part around the button is received by the press area.
- Pressing the press area calls the button's click notification as is. If the button is turned off or cannot be pressed, the press area follows.
- Follows the button's position, size and pivot every frame, so it stays matched even when the screen re-places the button.
- If a clipping node is set, clips the widened part so it does not go outside that node's screen rectangle. (the button's own area stays as is, so that areas outside the window or the scroll box are not pressed)
  Clipping is correct when the parent does not rotate.
- Usage: UIHitArea.attach(buttonNode, minimumSize) (call after the button is attached to its parent)

Multi-level bloom effect. (extracts the bright part at half size, blurs it while halving the size, then adds it back to the level above while doubling the size)
- Each level is half the size of the previous level. The first level (half the scene size) is the result. (getResultTexture)
- Extraction: from the average of four source samples, the part whose brightness (the largest of the three channels) exceeds the threshold. Within the knee width around the threshold it comes in smoothly. (setThreshold(threshold, knee))
- Downsampling is a dual filter mixing the center four and the four corners (one diagonal step), and upsampling is a nine-tap tent.
- With useFloatColor the targets are RGBA16F, so bright values above 1 are blurred as they are. (for HDR scenes, with RGBA8 they are clipped at 1)
- Usage: resize(scene width, height) → render(scene texture) → getResultTexture() is multiplied by the strength and added in the composite pass.
- Side effects: disables the depth test and blending, makes TEXTURE0 active, and changes the framebuffer binding. The blend function is restored to the previous one.

- Bakes the chosen characters in one font and one size into a glyph atlas (a single canvas), and when drawing text it cuts the glyphs out of the atlas.
  Every character uses the same image, so sprite batching is not broken. (unlike Text, which bakes a texture per string)
  Used where characters change often and the same characters are drawn many times, such as scores, damage numbers and clocks.
- Characters are counted by grapheme cluster (final consonants, combining marks, emoji sequences). Characters missing from the atlas are skipped, leaving a gap of half the font size.
- Adding characters with buildAtlas places all contained characters again on a new canvas. (so the positions of previously baked characters do not mismatch the new canvas)

Dynamic AABB tree. (2D, broad phase and spatial culling)
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change.
- A binary bounding volume hierarchy (BVH) of the same form as Box2D's b2DynamicTree. Each leaf is one proxy (box, category bits, user value).
  Insertion picks a sibling by the surface area heuristic (SAH, perimeter in 2D), and tree rotations (Kensler 2008) on the way up reduce the perimeter sum.
- Used not only for the physics broad phase but also for node culling (query with the screen box), touch picking (query with a point box) and ray picking (rayCast).
- Boxes are stored exactly as given. To avoid reinserting on every move, the caller gives a box with margin added (a fat box),
  and calls moveProxy only when the new box leaves the stored box. (2D physics does this)
- Same API and same math as experimental::spatial::DynamicTree of the Rust vanilla-engine. Inserting and removing in the same order gives the same tree shape in both engines.

Asynchronous load.

- If each game writes the version differently, the game composes the value received from readVersionData().

세이브 슬롯 관리.\n- 초안: 0.4.0 뒤 기능, API 가 바뀔 수:
Save slot manager.
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change.
- Each slot (slot) holds one piece of JSON data and a header (name, save time, version, preview image, size, game-defined metadata).
- Record form: "VSAVE1 <CRC-32 as 8 hex digits>\n<header JSON>\n<data JSON>". The CRC-32 is computed over the UTF-8 from the second line to the end.
  Same form as the Rust version (vanilla-engine), so the two engines read each other's saves. (when the storage uses the same keys)
- Atomic writes: each slot alternates between two keys (<namespace>.slot.<slot>.0 and .1). A new record goes to the key not holding the previous record, with the sequence number raised by one,
  and reading picks the one with the largest sequence number among those whose checksum matches. If writing is cut off (the tab closes, storage is full) or a record is corrupted, the previous save remains.
  Writing one key must either fully succeed or not happen at all, like localStorage.setItem.
- Migration: the data records its version (version), and when reading a version lower than the current one, functions registered with addMigration are called in turn for each version. (v → v + 1)
  Saves of a version higher than the current one (written by a newer game version) are not read.
- Autosave: register the slot, interval and a function giving the data with setAutosave, and call update every frame.
- Export and import: exportSlot gives JSON text containing the records as is, and importSlot checks the checksum and can import into another slot too.
- Cloud: plugging in a SaveCloudProvider with setCloudProvider uploads on every save, and pullFromCloud fetches and imports newer ones. (interface only)
- Results are { isSuccess, error (SaveGameError text or null), detail, ... } objects. (in place of the Result of the Rust version)

셰이더 미리 링크.\n- ShaderProgram 은 링크하자마자 결과를:
Shader pre-linking.
- ShaderProgram queries the result right after linking, so the main thread stalls until linking finishes. Building several shaders at once on first draw makes that frame stutter.
- At startup (during the logo, loading), linking the same sources in the background with KHR_parallel_shader_compile leaves them in the browser's program cache, so later when ShaderProgram builds the same sources it finishes quickly.
- Does nothing if the extension is absent. (Starting links without the extension can make later draw commands wait for the link and stall instead)
- Does not query link results, and deletes the programs and shaders once linked. (The cache remains, even if a source is wrong no error is raised here, the ShaderProgram at draw time reports it)
- Does not touch draw state (bound program, buffers, textures).
- Usage: new ShaderWarmer(webGL2RenderingContext, [{ vertexShader, fragmentShader, attributeLocationTable }]) then update() every frame.
  Attribute locations must be given the same as those passed to ShaderProgram to hit the cache.

소리. (배경음악과 효과음)\n\n엔진의 AudioManager(공유 A:
Sound. (background music and sound effects)

Uses the engine's AudioManager (shared AudioContext) and AudioAsset (MP3). Plays downloaded sound buffers with Web Audio. (does not synthesize sound, only plays files)
Takes a sound table. Each row is { id, path or paths, volume, minimumInterval, isMusic, maximumVoices, pitchVariation, playSeconds, fadeOutSeconds }.
  volume: per-sound volume. (0 ~ 1)  minimumInterval: interval before the same sound can play again. (seconds, so they do not pile up and get noisy)
  paths: a group of multiple recordings of the same sound. Picks one each time it plays, never the same as the one just before. (path if only one)
  maximumVoices: number of instances of the same sound that can play at once. (beyond that the oldest is cut off, if absent up to the total number of sound effects)
  pitchVariation: ratio by which the pitch varies on each play. (0.05 means ±5%, 0 if absent)
  playSeconds, fadeOutSeconds: plays only the first playSeconds seconds of a sound effect and fades it out over fadeOutSeconds seconds. (long files, to the end if absent or 0)

Volume: background music = music volume setting × music ratio (half volume for the pause window, etc.) × sound volume, sound effect = sound effect volume setting × sound volume × volume at call time (attenuation by distance, etc.).
Background music can be crossfaded (fadeSeconds), and the stopped position is remembered per sound so it can resume from there. (isResumed)
Mute takes precedence over the volume setting. If any one of the following applies, no sound plays regardless of the settings.
  - Platform mute. (the function given with setExternalMuteProvider, the platform SDK's mute setting, while a rewarded ad is shown, etc.)
  - The user's mute button. (setUserMuted)
  - Page hidden. (another tab, app switch)
  - The window loses focus on a touch-primary device. (blur, when the app starts going to the background)
    On iPhone the page-hidden notification arrives after the app has gone to the background, by which time audio freezes without stopping and the last sound chunk repeats.
    The window focus-loss notification arrives before that. On desktop, clicking outside the canvas (the outer page) also loses focus, so it is not followed there.
Platform mute is read every frame (update), and page hiding is applied at that moment. (frames stop when hidden)
While muted, the AudioContext is also stopped. (suspend, resume when unmuted) On iPhone, if an app switch or interstitial ad takes over a running AudioContext,
no sound plays even when it is woken on return. If it is stopped on its own beforehand, sound plays again on return.
If the AudioContext is still not running after unmuting, it tries to wake it at short intervals until it runs. (iPhone sometimes ignores the wake at the moment of returning to the app)

If allowed (setAutoplayAllowedProvider, allowed if not given), it tries to wake once even before a press. If blocked, it turns on at the first press as below.
Browsers do not allow sound before the person first presses. Since the engine creates and wakes the AudioContext on the first press,
the sound paths (music and sound effect buses, AudioBus) are created after that, and sound plays only while the AudioContext is running. (so sounds requested while stopped do not all play at once on wake)
Buses are retrieved with getMusicBus and getEffectBus. Players made from a bus (AudioBus.createAudioPlayer) also follow the volume setting and mute.
The volume setting is applied directly to the bus's GainNode. So values set with the bus's setVolume and mute last only until SoundSystem applies the volume again.
Sound files are downloaded in the background so they do not block play. Sounds not yet downloaded or that failed to download simply do not play.

Snap scroll view component.
- Inherits ScrollView, and snaps to the center of an item when a drag is released.
- Even when items differ in size, each item center snaps to the viewport center.
- Horizontal snap: setHorizontal(true), setVertical(false) (default)
- Vertical snap: setHorizontal(false), setVertical(true)

[Snap behavior]
- setSnapToNearest(false) : moves only one item per swipe. (default)
  While dragging, the offset never goes beyond one item on either side of the current one. On release, if the drag velocity is at least setVelocityThreshold
  it moves one item in that direction (fling), otherwise it moves when the dragged distance is at least the setPageChangeThreshold ratio of the neighbor item size.
- setSnapToNearest(true)  : snaps to the item nearest the dragged position. (The drag is not clamped to neighbor items, so it can pass several items)
- setVelocityThreshold(px/s): minimum velocity that decides the direction in one-item mode. (default: 200, pixels per second the scroll offset moved)

[Paging]
- pageTo(index, smooth): moves to the given index. smooth=true tweens, false moves immediately.

Sets sprite batching.
- When on, consecutive draws (images, shapes, text) using the same texture are accumulated with transform and color stored in the vertices, then drawn in a single draw call.
- When the texture, blend, clipping or swapped-in shader changes, or the buffer fills, everything accumulated so far is drawn, and the engine draws the rest at frame end.
- Gathering many images into one sheet (atlas) greatly reduces draw calls.
- When inserting a pass that handles WebGL directly (external renderer, etc.) with this on, call flushSpriteBatch() before it.

Heat haze effect component.
- Takes the canvas content drawn before the attached node, over the node's area, and applies a shimmering effect.
- Therefore the effect is visible only when attached to the node drawn last (topmost) in the scene. Child nodes are drawn over the effect.
- A component attached to a node, like ParticleSystem and TrailRenderer. The area uses the node's content size (contentSize) and pivot.
  If the node's content size is empty when attached, it is set to 300 x 300.
- Usage:
    const heatHazeEffect = node.addComponent(HeatHazeEffect);
    heatHazeEffect.setAmplitude(4);
- In the WebGL Graphic, it flushes the batch first, copies the screen bounding box of the node area (drawing buffer pixels) into a texture with copyTexSubImage2D,
  and redraws it shifted along a sine curve, one quad per line, as vertex color quads (drawColoredQuads). (same method as the Rust vanilla-engine)
- If the area goes off screen, the screen edge pixels are stretched. (CLAMP_TO_EDGE)
- The copied texture is a GL resource, so call destroy() when done with it.

- Form: { name, frameRate, bones: [{ name, parent, x, y, rotation, scaleX, scaleY, shearX, shearY, length }],
  slots: [{ name, bone, attachment, color: "#rrggbb(aa)", blendMode }], ik: [{ name, bones: [parent, child], target, bendPositive, mix }],
  skins: [{ name, attachments: { slot: { attachment: { type: "region" | "mesh", frame, ... } } } }],
  animations: { name: { duration, bones: { bone: { rotate, translate, scale, shear } }, slots: { slot: { color, attachment } }, drawOrder, events } } }
- Region attachment: x, y, rotation, scaleX, scaleY, width, height, pivotX, pivotY. Mesh attachment: vertices (relative to the slot bone), uvs, triangles, weights ([bone name, weight, ...] per vertex).
  The bound positions of weighted meshes are computed from the setup pose. (same form as Unity 2D Animation and DragonBones)
- Keys: { time (seconds), value or x, y or color or name, curve: "linear" | "stepped" | [x1, y1, x2, y2] }. The order of a draw order key is all slot names.

Input actions.
- Binds keys, gamepad buttons, and one side of gamepad axes to action names (strings the game defines, like "confirm", "left"). Several can be bound to one action, and it is pressed if any one of them is pressed.
- The engine's InputManager holds one (getInputActions) and calls update in tick at the start of the frame. The game only reads.
- Like the Unity Input System, it updates once in update at the start of the frame, and reads within that frame (readGamepadStick and readMoveAxis too) return the values recorded then. (same as the Rust engine)
- A key pressed and released between frames counts as pressed once in that frame. (InputManager.isKeyJustPressed)
- For an action with setRepeat, holding it makes isJustPressed true again at each interval after a wait. (menu selection)
- Axes subtract the dead zone (setDeadZone) and rescale the rest to 0 ~ 1. Sticks are filtered by length, bound axes by their one-side value.
- External sources (addSource) are where the game plugs in input the engine doesn't know (such as a platform SDK's pad). They are objects with the functions below.
    readActionValue(action) → a number 0 ~ 1 or a boolean. (pressed if 0.5 or more)
    readMoveAxis() → { x, y } or null. (optional, merged into readMoveAxis)
    readGamepadKind() → a GamepadKind value. (optional, in frames where this source provided input, records the last device as a gamepad of that kind)
- Keys are not listened to while typing in a text field. (turned off with setKeysIgnoredWhileTyping)

Auto tile. (rule tile)
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change.
- Same rules as RuleTile of Unity 2D Tilemap Extras. Each rule has conditions on the 8 surrounding cells (don't care, same auto tile, something else) and a tile value to place,
  and the tile of the first matching rule from the top is placed. If none matches, it is the default tile.
- Rule transforms: fixed, rotated (the conditions are rotated clockwise in 90 degree steps and on a match the tile is rotated by the same amount), mirror X, mirror Y, both.
  The order is the same as Unity. (fixed first, rotations 90, 180, 270, mirror both as XY, X, Y)
- Cells hold only tile values. Whether a cell is this auto tile is judged by whether its gid is the default tile or one of the rule tiles.
- The surroundings are the 8 cells of an orthogonal grid. (isometric uses the same cell math so it works as is, hexagonal neighbors are out of scope)

Clay model (GLB) reading and skeleton pose. (into toon 3D MeshBuilder vertex arrays, comes from webgame-rimminer)

Reads models painted with material colors. Also reads texture coordinates and material textures if present.
  - One part is one node, and a node's mesh has one primitive per color. Vertices have position and normal, plus joint indices and weights if there is a skeleton.
  - The material's baseColorFactor is a linear color so it is converted to sRGB and stored, and emissiveFactor, if present, is stored as glow. (if emissiveTexture exists, glow is passed only through the material range)
  - TEXCOORD_0, if present, is stored as uvData. A material range (materialRanges) is stored per primitive.
    { name material name, materialIndex, nodeName, indexStart, indexCount, extras material extras, alphaMode, alphaCutoff, baseColorFactor linear, emissiveFactor linear, baseColorImage, emissiveImage (index into images, -1 if none), hasUv }
    When painting separate sections within a part (accent color sections, display panels), pick by material name or extras and draw only that section with indexStart, indexCount of ToonRenderer.drawMesh.
  - Images are read with readGlbImages, decoded with decodeGlbImage and passed to ToonRenderer.createTexture.
  - In material extras, outline marks an outline shell (only back faces drawn), basic marks an unlit part.
    If outlineOptions is given, those shells are not stored, and a shell of uniform width per point is newly built from the body of nodes that have a ".outline" pair. (MeshBuilder.addTriangleShell)
  - If there is a skeleton (skin), reads the bone nodes and their inverse bind matrices, the animations and their extras (hitAt for strikes, loop "once" for play-once, etc.) together. The pose is computed by writeSkinPose.
  - Models whose parts are hidden or painted separately (like a cluster of several crystals) are read per node with readGlbNodeArrays.
    Node extras (pivot where doors and legs rotate, etc.) are stored together as that part's extras.
  - For a skinned model read as one chunk (like a vehicle), node extras, part positions and followed bones are read separately with readGlbNodeInfos.
The engine's GLB reader is tied up inside the engine's PBR model (SkinnedModel), so only the vertex arrays for toon drawing are extracted here.

Reading clay models (GLB) and skeleton poses. (Into toon 3D MeshBuilder vertex arrays, came from webgame-rimminer)

Reads models painted with material colors. Texture coordinates and material textures are read too if present.
  - One part is one node, and a node's mesh is one primitive per color. Vertices are position and normal, plus joint indices and weights if there is a skeleton.
  - The material's baseColorFactor is a linear color, so it is converted to sRGB, and emissiveFactor, if present, is stored as glow. (If there is an emissiveTexture, glow is passed only through the material range)
  - TEXCOORD_0, if present, goes into uvData and TEXCOORD_1 into uv1Data (second UV, angel ring). A material range (materialRanges) is stored per primitive.
    { name material name, materialIndex, nodeName, indexStart, indexCount, extras material extras, alphaMode, alphaCutoff, baseColorFactor linear, emissiveFactor linear, baseColorImage, emissiveImage (images order, -1 if none), hasUv }
    When painting split areas inside a part (accent color areas, display panels), pick them by material name or extras and draw only that area with indexStart and indexCount of ToonRenderer.drawMesh.
  - Images are read with readGlbImages, decoded with decodeGlbImage and passed to ToonRenderer.createTexture.
  - outline in material extras is an outline shell (only back faces drawn), and basic is a part that does not receive light.
    If outlineOptions is given, that shell is not stored, and a shell of uniform thickness per point is newly built from the body of each node that has a ".outline" pair. (MeshBuilder.addTriangleShell)
  - If there is a skeleton (skin), the joint nodes and their inverse bind matrices, the animations and their extras (hitAt of an attack, loop "once" that plays only once, and so on) are read together. Poses are computed by writeSkinPose.
  - Models whose parts are hidden or painted separately (like a cluster of several crystals) are read per node with readGlbNodeArrays.
    Node extras (pivot where doors and legs rotate, and so on) are stored as that part's extras.
  - For a skeletal model read as one lump (like a vehicle), node extras, part positions and the joints they follow are read separately with readGlbNodeInfos.
The engine's GLB reader is tied inside the engine's PBR model (SkinnedModel), so only the vertex arrays used for toon drawing are extracted here.

- Dims the whole area (presses do not pass through to what is behind) and shows a panel in the center. The dim also covers the safe area (setViewBleed).
- The panel widens to fit the area's width but does not exceed maximumWidth. Its height is the value returned by layoutContent, and if it is larger than the area the whole panel is scaled down.

  (setSiblingIndex(0) for things placed behind the panel), and overrides layoutPanel to fit them to the panel size. The default panel Paint is changed or turned off via getPanelPaint().
  For the motion shape (a panel rising from below, etc.), override applyMotion.
- The derived class places the content inside the panel in layoutContent(panelWidth) and returns the panel's height. (default is the setPanelHeight value)

Detects slow devices. (measures frame intervals for the first few seconds, used to automatically turn on a lightweight path that disables heavy effects)
- After measuring starts and the wait seconds pass, looks at each frame's interval during the measure seconds. (the first few seconds stutter while models and images load)
- If frames exceeding the slow multiple of the target interval (one frame at the max frame rate, or one frame at 60 if unlimited) make up at least the slow fraction, it is a slow device.
  - Why 1.4 times rather than one frame: a 90 Hz screen with max 60 has the engine draw every other refresh, so the interval is always 22 ms, and that is not the device being slow.
  - On 60 Hz and 120 Hz screens, a frame that missed one refresh (33 ms, 25 ms) counts as slow. One in four means below 48 fps.
- Once judged a slow device, it does not measure again. If the window is hidden before measuring finishes, restart() measures again from the start.
  If not slow, measureAgain() can measure once more in a heavy scene.
- Does not import the engine or the browser. The caller passes the frame interval and max frame rate.

Camera gestures. (gestures that rotate, pan and zoom a 3D board or map, mouse right and middle button drag, two fingers)
- The engine's input only passes press, drag and release of one finger (or any mouse button). Rotate, pan and zoom gestures are outside that, so the canvas DOM events are read separately. (the engine's behavior is left as is)
  - Dragging with the right mouse button held: rotates by the horizontal drag (the screen width is one full turn) and tilts by the vertical drag. Releasing without dragging is a right click.
  - Dragging with the middle mouse button held: pans.
  - Two fingers: dragging in the same direction pans, pinching in and out zooms in and out around the midpoint of the two fingers, and twisting past the twist threshold rotates. (prevents slight rotation while pinch-zooming)
- The wheel is passed by the engine. Here it only records whether Ctrl was held. (laptop touchpad pinches also arrive as Ctrl wheel)
- During a gesture, isGestureActive signals not to use the presses and releases passed by the engine for gameplay.
- The accumulated amounts (pan, rotate, tilt, zoom) are taken out every frame with take. Pan is in view units, rotate and tilt in radians, zoom is a ratio to multiply.
- Also reads whether the last input was a finger or a mouse. Mouse events the browser emulates right after a finger is lifted are ignored.
- Constructing attaches events to the engine's canvas. When done, dispose().

Tilemap.
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change.
- A component attached to a node. The top left of the node's content area is the map's (0, 0), and layers (TilemapLayer) are drawn in the order they were added.
- There are four orientations: orthogonal (orthogonal), isometric (isometric, diamond), staggered (staggered, staggered isometric) and hexagonal (hexagonal).
  Coordinate conversion, draw order, tile image alignment (the cell's bottom left), flips and rotations use the same math as the Tiled renderer (libtiled).
- Each layer chunk (chunk) is checked for overlap with the screen and skipped entirely if it does not overlap. Overlapping chunks append tiles that use the same image to a vertex buffer,
  drawing with one Graphic.drawVertices call only when the image changes or the buffer fills. (Chunk mode of Unity TilemapRenderer)
  Individual mode draws in the cell order of the whole map across chunks. (the order is exact when large tiles overlap neighboring chunks)
- Tile animation runs on one clock advanced by tick, so all cells animate together. (same as Tiled)
- Collision shapes do not depend on physics. readCellCollisionShapes returns map-coordinate shapes (TileCollisionShape) with each cell's flip, rotation and offset applied.

- In drag mode, delivers only to the ScrollView.
- If not in drag mode, there is a ScrollView, and the threshold is exceeded, switches modes:
  (1) if a delayed press is pending, cancels it (not delivered at all),
      if press was already delivered, touchCancel to the hit node,
  (2) touchPress (initial position) → touchMove (current position) to the ScrollView.
- Otherwise touchMove to the hit node. However, if press has not been delivered yet,
  touchMove is not delivered either.

Touch recognizer.
- Extends TouchRaycaster to do UIKit-style gesture recognition.
- Finds the node with a UIScrollView in the pressed node's parent chain in advance,
  and when the drag threshold is exceeded:
    1) sends touchCancel to the pressed node to cancel the click
    2) sends touchPress (initial press position) → touchMove (current) to the ScrollView above,
       in order, to hand over the scroll.
- Within the threshold, sends touch* only to the pressed node. (Behaves like a basic button)
- If the ScrollView has setPassesCrossAxisDrag(true), a finger dragged more along the non-scrolling axis
  is not handed over. The pending press is sent right away to the hit node, and the following moves are also
  sent to the hit node. (When dragging a slider inside a scroll horizontally)
- When a parent has a ScrollView, delivery of touchPress to the hit node is delayed by
  DELAY_PRESS_MS. If it turns out to be a drag meanwhile, press is never delivered, so
  "cancel during press transition" does not occur. For a short tap, at release time
  the pending press is fired immediately and release is sent right after to compensate.

- Off-screen culling: tests the model's bounding sphere against the view-projection frustum and skips drawing if outside. (instances are culled one by one and only the rest are uploaded)
- Shadows: cast into a ShadowMap with beginShadowPass and drawMesh, received with setShadow. (3x3 PCF, the bias is the texel-unit value of ShadowMap.setBias multiplied by the texel size and slope)
  Even when not receiving shadows, a 1x1 comparison depth texture is bound to the shadow unit. (if a sampler2DShadow unit has no depth texture the Mac driver reports it, and if a color texture is bound WebGL refuses to draw)
- HDR: setHdrOutput(true) outputs linear color without gamma. Draw into a float render target (ToonPostProcess) and finish with bloom and tone mapping.

- Draw options (options, the defaults give the same picture as before):
  tintColor [r, g, b, a] sRGB and alpha. If tintAmount (0 ~ 1) is given, the tint is mixed in sRGB instead of multiplied. (Hit flash, broken red)
  glowScale multiplier of vertex glow (default 1), colorScale multiplier of the final linear color (default 1, darkens a mirrored image), emissiveColor [r, g, b] sRGB and emissiveIntensity (linear multiplier, default 1, color default black).
  baseColorTexture (multiplied by the base color, alpha into opacity), emissiveTexture (multiplied by the glow color), uvTransform [u offset, v offset, u scale, v scale] (offset and scale of KHR_texture_transform).
  decalTexture covers the base color with alpha (color = texture x decalColor). It glows in that color by decalEmission. decalUvTransform picks one cell of an atlas.
  alphaCutoff discards pixels whose opacity is below it. (0 turns it off, glTF MASK)
  blendMode: ToonBlendMode.alpha (default, straight alpha), premultiplied (premultiplied alpha), additive (add). Anything other than alpha is drawn as transparent.
  softEdge multiplies pow(|dot(N, V)|, softEdge) into the opacity to thin the edges. (0 turns it off, Fresnel form)
  isMirrored draws with the winding flipped. If not given, it flips by itself when the determinant of the model matrix is negative. If the view matrix is mirrored, that flip is added too.
  indexStart, indexCount draw only that span of the body vertex indices. (GLB material ranges, hidden parts) outlineIndexStart, outlineIndexCount are for the outline shell.
  material (ToonMaterial), textures ({ uniform name: texture }), onBeforeDraw(program, webGL2RenderingContext, ToonProgramKind) are extension points. (toonmaterial.js header)
  lightSet (ToonLightSet) is the light set of that draw.
  If receivesShadow (default true) is false, the sun's shadow is not looked up. shadeOffset is added to the received light amount to move the shade boundary. (Vertex color threshold of Guilty Gear Xrd, Shading Grade Map form of the Unity Toon Shader)
  specularScale, rimScale (default 1) are the highlight and rim multipliers of that draw. (0 means none, strength per material)
  matcapTexture is a matcap read with the view-space normal. matcapStrength (default 1), matcapBlend (ToonMatcapBlend.multiply default, add)
  outlineColor [r, g, b, a] sRGB is the shell outline color of that draw (setOutlineColor if not given), outlineWidthScale (default 1) is the multiplier of the built thickness.
  outlineOffsetZ (default 0) is the world length the shell is pushed away from the camera. (So it does not show in front of the body, Offset Z of the Unity Toon Shader)
  angelRingTexture is the angel ring texture. u is the x of the view-space normal, v is the y of the second UV mixed with the y of the view normal by angelRingOffsetV (default 0.3). (Angel Ring of the Unity Toon Shader)
  angelRingColor [r, g, b] (linear multiplier, default white), angelRingOffsetU (0 ~ 0.5, default 0), isAngelRingAlpha (default false adds, true covers with the texture alpha)
  The angel ring UV is rotated back by the camera roll. (readCameraRoll, Camera Rolling Stabilizer of the Unity Toon Shader, the ring stays on the head even when the camera is tilted)
  lineId, hasScreenOutline, hasCreaseLine are values ToonDrawQueue passes to the screen-space outline. (The renderer does not read them)
- Outline shell (inverted hull): uploads the base position and push direction (built thickness, the averaged normal of the same position) of the shell MeshBuilder built, and the shader pushes it by outlineWidthScale and draws only back faces.
  If setOutlineDistanceScale(reference distance, minimum scale, maximum scale) is given, distance to the camera / reference distance is multiplied into the thickness to keep the screen thickness. (Perspective only)
  If setOutlineFadeDistance(near distance, far distance) is given, the thickness goes to 0 as the distance from the model position to the camera approaches the far distance. (smoothstep, Nearest and Farthest Distance of the Unity Toon Shader)
  The shell color is multiplied by the sun color when the outline light color usage of the light set is on (default). (Divided by its intensity when the intensity is 1 or more, same as the Unity Toon Shader outline)
- Skeleton: the joint matrices computed by writeSkinPose are passed to drawMesh. (Up to TOON_MAXIMUM_JOINTS)
- GPU instancing: drawMeshInstanced draws many copies of the same model at once with a matrix and tint per instance. (Both body and outline, culled and uploaded on every draw)
  Long-lived instances build a persistent buffer with createInstanceLayout and createInstanceBuffer and are drawn with drawMeshInstanceBuffer. (Culled as a whole by the bounds of the entire buffer, the material vertex chunk reads user attributes)
  To change it use updateInstanceBuffer (whole) or updateInstanceBufferRange (part, bufferSubData). The body, outline shell, shadows and the screen-space outline's line target share the same GPU buffer.
- Off-screen culling: the model's bounding sphere is tested against the frustum of view and projection and is not drawn if outside. (Instances are culled one by one and only the remaining ones are uploaded)
- Shadows: cast into a ShadowMap with beginShadowPass and drawMesh, received with setShadow. (3x3 PCF, the bias is the texel-unit value of ShadowMap.setBias multiplied by the texel size and slope)
  Point light and spotlight shadows are cast into a ShadowAtlas with beginShadowAtlasPass and, per tile, setShadowAtlasTile and drawMesh, and received with setLocalShadows. (A point light uses six cube tiles, a spotlight one perspective tile)
  The shadow is multiplied into that light's received amount and goes into the shade ramp. (Same form as the sun) Only point lights with castsShadow true get tiles. (Up to SHADOW_ATLAS_MAXIMUM_LIGHTS)
  Even when shadows are not received, a 1x1 comparison depth texture is bound to both shadow units. (Without a depth texture on a sampler2DShadow unit the Mac driver reports it, and if a color texture is bound WebGL refuses to draw)
- HDR: setHdrOutput(true) outputs linear color without gamma. Draw into a float render target (ToonPostProcess) and finish with bloom and tone mapping.
- Use: createMesh(arrays) → every frame beginFrame(view and projection) → drawMesh / drawMeshInstanced → endFrame() → deleteMesh when done.
  beginFrame notes the previous draw state (blend, depth, face culling, program, vertex array) and turns on depth test and face culling, and endFrame restores the noted state.
  (When inserted between engine 2D drawing, call Graphic.flushBatch before it)
  beginFrameWithMatrices(view, projection) starts with two matrices. (Orthographic or raw matrix camera) The camera position and view rotation (highlight, rim, soft edge, matcap) are read from the view and projection.
- Per program, frame values (view and projection, camera, shadow, HDR) and the light set are uploaded only when changed. Only values that change per draw (model matrix, tint, textures) are uploaded every time.
- readProgramSources(material, instanceLayout) gives the sources to pass to ShaderWarmer.
- Drawing inside a node rectangle: if setScreenRect(x, y, width, height) is given, beginFrame moves the clip space of view and projection into that rectangle and cuts the outside with the scissor.
  The rectangle is in pixels inside the viewport at beginFrame (usually the whole drawing buffer) with the top left as the origin. (The position computed with graphic.getTransformMatrix in a 2D node's draw)
  Off-screen culling uses the frustum before the move. endFrame releases the scissor. Match the camera aspect ratio to the rectangle's ratio. (Camera3D.setAspectRatio)
- beginFrameWithCamera(Camera3D) calls beginFrame with the camera's view and projection. It uses the same camera as the 2D display (Camera3D.projectToView).
- drawMeshOutline draws only the outline shell. (When ToonDrawQueue draws all outlines together after all opaque bodies, drawn counts are not counted)
- Textures: createTexture(image or { width, height, data }, { isMipmapped, isRepeated, isFiltered }) builds an RGBA texture. UV (0, 0) is the top left of the image. (Same as glTF)
- Texture units: point light shadow atlas 0, ramp 1, matcap 2, sun shadow 3, base color 4, glow 5, decal 6, angel ring 7, material 8 ~ 15. beginFrame notes the binding of unit 0 and endFrame restores it.
- Second UV: if the arrays have uv1Data, vertexUv is four values (UV, second UV). Shader chunks read it as ToonSurface.uv1. ((0, 1) if none)
- Light color usage (setLightColorUsage), shade-side rim (setShadeRimLight) and light intensity limit (setLightIntensityLimited) live in the light set (ToonLightSet).

The same context as the toon renderer.
툰 머티리얼. (ToonRenderer 의 몸 셰이더에 끼울 셰이더 조각: Toon material. (shader chunks inserted into ToonRenderer's body shader, the per-game extension point)

Toon material. (Shader chunks inserted into ToonRenderer's body shader, the per-game extension point)
- Only patterns and effects that the engine's standard features (textures, light, tint, blending) cannot do go into chunks. Slots without a chunk get the engine's empty functions.
- uniformChunk: goes into the top slot of the fragment shader. Write uniforms, constants, functions and the ins exported by the vertex chunk.
- surfaceChunk: defines void applySurface(inout ToonSurface surface). The engine calls it after computing the vertex color, textures and decal, before tint and light.
  ToonSurface { vec3 baseColor (sRGB), float alpha, vec3 emission (linear), vec3 normal (world, unit), float glow (vertex glow), bool isUnlit,
                vec4 detail (vertex pattern number and pattern color), vec2 uv, vec2 uv1 (second UV, (0, 1) if none), vec3 localPosition (model coordinates), vec3 worldPosition, vec3 viewDirection (from the surface toward the camera, unit),
                float shadeOffset (value added to the received light amount, moves the shade boundary), float specularMask (highlight multiplier), float rimMask (rim light multiplier) }
- lightChunk: defines void applyLight(ToonSurface surface, inout ToonLighting lighting). The engine calls it after gathering the sun, ambient light, fill, point lights and spotlights, highlight and rim, before combining.
  ToonLighting { vec3 irradiance (light multiplied into the base color, after the shade ramp), vec3 specular (highlight to add), vec3 rim (rim light to add), float shadow (0 ~ 1), float sunLevel (brightness level of the received sun 0 ~ 1) }
  Combining is base color x irradiance + specular x specularMask + rim x rimMask + glow.
- vertexChunk: goes into the top slot of the vertex shaders (all three: body, outline, shadow depth) and defines void applyVertex(inout ToonVertex vertex). Called before moving into world space.
  ToonVertex { vec3 localPosition, vec3 localNormal, vec3 color, vec2 material, vec4 detail, vec2 uv, vec2 uv1, vec4 tint, mat4 modelMatrix }
  User attributes of the instance layout (ToonInstanceLayout) are read as ins of that name. Since it goes into all three, do not use outs that exist only in the body. (Use the fields of vertex instead of vertex attribute names)
  Normals are moved by mat3(modelMatrix). If the scale is not uniform, divide localNormal by the square of that scale beforehand.
- The shader has the engine's toLinear(vec3) and RECIPROCAL_PI.
- Textures are passed with the draw's options.textures ({ uniform name: texture }). The engine binds them in order to units it does not use (from 8, up to TOON_MAXIMUM_MATERIAL_TEXTURES) and puts the unit into the sampler2D uniform of that name.
- Uniforms that differ per draw are written in options.onBeforeDraw(program, webGL2RenderingContext). The engine rewrites its own uniforms, so write only the material's.

- Only patterns or effects that the engine's standard features (texture, light, tint, blending) cannot do go into chunks. Slots without a chunk get the engine's empty function.

- surfaceChunk: defines void applySurface(inout ToonSurface surface). Called after the engine computes the vertex color, texture and decals, before tint and light.
  ToonSurface { vec3 baseColor (sRGB), float alpha, vec3 emission (linear), vec3 normal (world, unit), float glow (vertex glow), bool isUnlit,
                vec4 detail (vertex pattern index and pattern color), vec2 uv, vec3 localPosition (model coordinates), vec3 worldPosition, vec3 viewDirection (from the surface toward the camera, unit) }
- lightChunk: defines void applyLight(ToonSurface surface, inout ToonLighting lighting). Called after the engine gathers the sun, ambient, fill, rim, point lights and specular, before combining them.

  ToonVertex { vec3 localPosition, vec3 localNormal, vec3 color, vec2 material, vec4 detail, vec2 uv, vec4 tint, mat4 modelMatrix }
  User attributes of the instance layout (ToonInstanceLayout) are read as ins of that name. Since it goes into all three, do not use outs that exist only in the body. (use the fields of vertex instead of the vertex attribute names)
  Normals are transformed with mat3(modelMatrix). If the scale is not uniform, divide localNormal by the square of that scale beforehand.
- The shader has the engine's toLinear(vec3) and RECIPROCAL_PI.
- Textures are passed with the draw's options.textures ({ uniform name: texture }). The engine binds them in order to the units it does not use (from 7) and puts the unit into the sampler2D uniform of that name.

툰 빛 묶음. (ToonRenderer 가 몸을 칠할 빛 값을 한 덩어리: Toon light set. (holds as one bundle the light values ToonRenderer uses to shade bodies)

Toon light set. (holds as one bundle the light values ToonRenderer uses to shade bodies)
- The renderer holds one default set, and the renderer's light settings such as setLight modify that set. A different set can be given per draw with options.lightSet. (when the board and the models have different lighting)
- Sun: the direction (sunDirection) is the way the light travels. It is the direction from the sun to the surface, the opposite of the direction pointing from the surface toward the sun. (the direction from position to target of a three.js DirectionalLight)
  The share a surface receives is max(dot(N, -sunDirection), 0). Shining straight down from above is [0, -1, 0].
- Ambient: mixes the sky color and ground color by the normal's up and down (N.y x 0.5 + 0.5). (hemisphere light)
- Fill light (fill): a second directional light that does not receive shadows. Its direction means the same as the sun's. With the default color 0 it is absent.
- Rim light (rim): an edge light pow(1 - max(dot(N, V), 0), power) that grows stronger as the normal turns away from the view direction. Like light, it is multiplied by the base color. With the default strength 0 it is absent.
- Specular: the sun's Blinn-Phong pow(max(dot(N, H), 0), exponent) x strength. It receives shadows. With the default 0 it is absent.
- Point lights: up to TOON_MAXIMUM_POINT_LIGHTS. { position, color (linear), intensity, range, decay, rangeExponent, wrap }
  Attenuation is window x distance attenuation. The window is (1 - (distance / range)^rangeExponent) clamped to 0 ~ 1 and squared if range is greater than 0, and 1 if it is 0. Distance attenuation is 1 / max(distance^decay, 0.01) if decay is greater than 0, and 1 if it is 0.
  The defaults (decay 2, rangeExponent 4) are the point light form of three.js, Unreal and Godot 4. With decay 0 and rangeExponent 1 it becomes the (1 - distance / range)^2 form (Godot 3's attenuation 1).
  The received share is wrap light (dot(N, L) + wrap) / (1 + wrap). (0 is Lambert, the wrap lighting of GPU Gems 1)
- Bands: setBandCount(n) rounds the share received from the sun into n steps. (0 is smooth, the default so far)
  setBandRamp(thresholds, values, half Lambert) splits the share by the thresholds and uses each step's value. With half Lambert, dot x 0.5 + 0.5 is compared to the thresholds, otherwise max(dot, 0). If there is a ramp, the band count is not used. The same bands also apply to the share received from point lights.
- Light model: if setLightModel({ isEnergyNormalized }) is true, base color x light is divided by π. (the textbook Lambert BRDF, the same convention as three.js physical lights, which give light intensity as illuminance, and glTF lights)
  In that case specular is multiplied by the normalized Blinn-Phong factor (exponent + 8) / 8π. With the default false it is base color x light as before.
- All colors are linear colors. (they may exceed 1 for HDR)
- Modifying it raises the version number (getVersion). The renderer does not re-upload if the set and version number are the same.
툰 빛 묶음. (ToonRenderer 가 몸을 칠할 빛과 툰 빛 반응을: Toon light set. (Holds as one bundle the lights ToonRenderer uses to shade bodies and the toon light response)

Toon light set. (Holds as one bundle the lights ToonRenderer uses to shade bodies and the toon light response)
- The renderer holds one default set, and the renderer's light settings such as setLight change that set. Another set can be given per draw with options.lightSet. (When the shade color differs per material)
- Sun (key light): the direction (sunDirection) is the way the light travels. It is the opposite of the direction from the surface toward the sun. ([0, -1, 0] when shining down from above) It receives shadows.
- Ambient light: sky color and ground color are mixed by the up and down of the normal (N.y x 0.5 + 0.5). (Hemisphere light)
- Shade ramp (cel shading): the received light amount x is laid against the ramp to pick the color. x is dot(N, L) x 0.5 + 0.5 for half Lambert, otherwise max(dot(N, L), 0),
  and after adding the draw's shadeOffset, for the sun it is multiplied by the shadow (received amount 0 ~ 1). (Shadows enter as the shade color rather than black, System Shadows of the Unity Toon Shader)
  The ramp has a position, color (linear multiplier) and softness per cell (stop). The color of cell i transitions from the previous cell's color as x rises from (position - softness) to the position. (Step and Feather of the Unity Toon Shader)
  If the softness is smaller than one pixel width (fwidth), it is held at that width so the boundary does not stair-step.
  setShade builds the ramp from three, base, 1st shade and 2nd shade (Base, 1st Shade, 2nd Shade of the Unity Toon Shader), setShadeRamp from cells directly, setBandCount from even cells, setBandRamp from gray cells.
  If setRampTexture is given, the horizontal of that texture (x as u, v is 0.5) is read instead of cells. (The warp of Team Fortress 2, the ramp textures of Genshin and Honkai)
  Without cells (clearShadeRamp, setBandCount(0)) it is smooth Lambert.
- Per light: the sun receives the whole ramp color so the shade also takes on the sun's color. The fill light, point lights and spotlights receive the ramp's brightness level (bottom cell 0, top cell 1) and do not light faces turned away.
- Fill light (fill): a second directional light that receives no shadow. The direction means the same as the sun. With the default color 0 there is none.
- Highlight (specular): Blinn-Phong pow(max(dot(N, H), 0), exponent), from a hard spot cut at 0.5 (softness 0) to the plain soft light (softness 1). Color x strength x light color x received light level.
  It appears for the sun, point lights and spotlights alike. With the default strength 0 there is none.
- Rim light (rim): pow(1 - max(dot(N, V), 0), power), from a hard rim cut at 0.5 (softness 0) to a soft rim (1). If lightMask is 1, only on the side receiving the sun. Added regardless of the base color.
  The shade-side rim (setShadeRimLight) adds the same rim on the side facing away from the sun by (rim - (dot(N, L) x 0.5 + 0.5)). (Antipodean (Ap) Rim Light of the Unity Toon Shader)
- Light color usage (setLightColorUsage): chooses per color whether the light color is multiplied. When off, that color receives only the light's intensity (0.299 R + 0.587 G + 0.114 B), and the rim, matcap, angel ring and outline receive no light. (Is_LightColor_* of the Unity Toon Shader, all on by default)
- Light intensity limit (setLightIntensityLimited): limits what each light gives to 1. The sun and fill light are clamped to 1 per channel, and point lights and spotlights are divided by the intensity of their color with attenuation applied when it exceeds 1.
  (Limit Light Intensity of the Unity Toon Shader, on by default) Turn it off to use strong lights for HDR bloom.
  When porting an old game shader (one that did not limit light intensity), or when using point lights above intensity 1 or HDR bloom, use setLightIntensityLimited(false).
- Point lights and spotlights: up to TOON_MAXIMUM_POINT_LIGHTS. { position, color (linear), intensity, range, decay, rangeExponent, wrap, direction, innerConeAngle, outerConeAngle, castsShadow, shadowNear }
  Lights with castsShadow true get shadow tiles from ShadowAtlas.updateLights. (Six cube faces for a point light, one perspective tile for a spotlight, the far distance is range, the near distance is shadowNear default 0.05)
  Attenuation is window x distance attenuation. The window is (1 - (distance / range)^rangeExponent) clamped to 0 ~ 1 and squared if range is above 0, and 1 if 0. Distance attenuation is 1 / max(distance^decay, 0.01) if decay is above 0, and 1 if 0.
  The default (decay 2, rangeExponent 4) is the point light form of three.js, Unreal and Godot 4.
  Giving direction (the way the light travels) makes a spotlight. Angular attenuation is the square of clamp(cos angle x scale + offset, 0, 1) in the glTF KHR_lights_punctual form. (innerConeAngle default 0, outerConeAngle default π/4, radians)
  The received amount is the wrap (dot(N, L) + wrap) / (1 + wrap). (0 is Lambert, the wrap lighting of GPU Gems 1)
- Light model: if setLightModel({ isEnergyNormalized }) is true, base color x light is divided by π and the highlight is multiplied by (exponent + 8) / 8π. (The convention of giving physical light intensity as illuminance)
- All colors are linear colors. (They may exceed 1 for HDR) Ramp textures are treated as sRGB and read converted to linear.
- Each change raises the version number (getVersion). The renderer does not upload again if the set and version number are the same.

툰 화면 공간 바깥선. (노멀, 선 번호, 깊이를 선의 판에 그리고 한: Toon screen-space outline. (Draws normals, line IDs and depth into the line target, writes a mask in one sweep, then blends onto the screen)

Toon screen-space outline. (Draws normals, line IDs and depth into the line target, writes a mask in one sweep, then blends onto the screen)
- Draws ToonRenderer's createMesh result once more with the same matrices to write IDs. Can be used together with the shell outline (ToonRenderer).
- Where lines appear: outside the silhouette of what is in front, where it touches a different ID (the far side, or the larger ID if the depths are nearly equal), and where faces within one ID bend more than the crease angle.
  Lines are not drawn where the same IDs touch. Which model and which part (indexStart, indexCount range) gets which ID is decided by the caller.
- Width: world length or pixels via setWidth. Computed in line target pixels and never goes below one pixel.
- Depth: tells orthographic and perspective apart by the projection matrix. Perspective unpacks depth with the near and far planes and compares distances (meters).
- Cost: setResolutionScale shrinks the line target to a fraction of the drawing area (the mask is smoothly upscaled when blending), setSampleCount reduces the number of neighbors sampled (lite path 4, 2).
- Usage: every frame beginLineIds(view, projection) → drawMesh / drawMeshInstanced → endLineIds() (computes up to the mask) → draw toon bodies → drawOutline().
  beginLineIds records the current viewport as the drawing area and builds the line target to fit that size. endLineIds restores the framebuffer, viewport and state.
  (When inserting between engine 2D draws, call Graphic.flushSpriteBatch before that)
툰 화면 공간 바깥선. (노멀, 선 번호, 깊이를 선의 판에 그리고, 바: Toon screen-space outline. (Draws normals, line IDs and depth into the line target, picks lines at the boundaries between direct neighbors, widens them with jump flooding, then computes coverage from distance and blends)

Toon screen-space outline. (Draws normals, line IDs and depth into the line target, picks lines at the boundaries between direct neighbors, widens them with jump flooding, then computes coverage from distance and blends)
- Line target: draws the result of ToonRenderer's createMesh once more with the same matrices and writes the normal (octahedral encoding), line ID (14 bits), flags (whether the silhouette line and crease line are on) and depth.
- Picking: each boundary between a pixel and its four direct neighbors is looked at once. A line stands not on a pixel but in the middle of the boundary between pixels. (The same boundary is not drawn twice)
  A silhouette line is where it touches empty space (the silhouette), where it touches a different ID, or where, even with the same ID, the two are farther apart than the depth threshold from each other's tangent plane (occluded silhouette).
  A crease line is where two neighboring normals within the same ID open wider than the crease angle. Since only normals one pixel apart are compared, no band appears around the silhouette of round surfaces or on slanted surfaces.
  Depth is compared as tangent plane distance, so no false lines appear on a floor seen at a grazing angle. Twice the pixel size at that depth is added to the threshold so distant things mean the same.
- Widening: the distance to the boundary segments is spread with jump flooding. The step count is log2 regardless of thickness, and silhouette and crease lines are spread separately to give separate thicknesses.
- Blending: each pixel of the drawing area is covered by clamp(thickness / 2 - distance + 0.5, 0, 1) from the distance to the nearest boundary. (Soft edges, and no stairs or dotted lines even when the widening target is reduced)
- Per model: if hasScreenOutline of drawMesh is false, that model produces no line and only hides lines behind it. If hasCreaseLine is false, only crease lines are turned off.
- Thickness: the thickness of setWidth and setCrease is the thickness of one line. (Half on each side of the boundary) The unit is ToonOutlineWidthUnit, and it does not go below one pixel.
- Depth: orthographic and perspective are told apart by the projection matrix, and depth is unpacked into view-space position for comparison. (Projections whose clip x and y were moved, like a screen rectangle, also work)
- Cost: setResolutionScale reduces the widening (jump flooding) target. (The light path for phones) The line target and seeds stay at drawing area resolution, so line positions do not change when reduced.
- Use: every frame beginLineIds(view, projection) → drawMesh / drawMeshInstanced → endLineIds() (computes seeds and widening) → draw the toon bodies → drawOutline().
  beginLineIds notes the current viewport as the drawing area and builds the line target to fit its size. endLineIds and drawOutline restore the framebuffer, viewport and state.
  If handed over with ToonDrawQueue.setScreenOutline, the draw queue does this sequence by itself. (When inserted between engine 2D drawing, call Graphic.flushBatch before it)

- Engine.alert, Engine.confirm and Engine.prompt call the browser functions and return a ModalDialogHandle. (same as the Rust Engine::alert, confirm and prompt)
- The browser shows the dialog and stops the page until answered, then the returned value goes into the handle. (it finishes on the spot, same as the Rust web version)

- The awaitable forms are Engine.alertAsync, confirmAsync and promptAsync.
- Where the browser functions do not exist (node), alert finishes as confirmed, and confirm and prompt finish as cancelled.

입력 필드 (캔버스 기반).\n- 텍스트 렌더링은 UILabel 자식 노:
Input field (canvas based).
- Text rendering uses two UILabel child nodes (value label + placeholder label).
- Click/drag/cursor movement/selection are all handled directly on the canvas side.
- Using a DOM <input> is optional (setUseDOMInput, default false). Korean IME /
  mobile soft keyboard / system clipboard work only when true. When false, the keyboard is handled directly, mostly ASCII.
- Context menu on right click (cut / copy / paste / select all). Direct-touch fields (setUseDirectTouch) also get this menu instead of the browser edit-field menu.
- Cursor movement and Delete work per grapheme cluster like Chrome, Backspace removes one code point like Blink's BackspaceStateMachine (emoji sequences as a whole).
- With DOM input, a mouse double click selects a word (with trailing whitespace on Windows) and a triple click selects all text, like a Chrome text field. (The click count is the mousedown detail)
- In canvas mode, word movement and deletion use Ctrl on Windows and Linux and Option on Mac with the left and right arrows, Backspace and Delete, like Chrome. (Blink NextWordPosition, PreviousWordPosition)
- Undo and redo are handled by an engine history in both modes. (The same Blink grouping rules as TextEditBuffer in the Rust edition: consecutively typed characters undo at once, moving the cursor or changing the selection breaks the group,
  a new edit clears the redo list, setText clears the lists) Keys are Ctrl (Cmd on Mac) + Z, Ctrl (Cmd on Mac) + Shift + Z, Ctrl + Y on Windows and Linux, and also Alt + Backspace on Windows.
  DOM input blocks the browser's undo keys and historyUndo, historyRedo and uses the engine history. It does not undo during IME composition.
