Toon draw queue. (Holds the models to draw in a frame, then draws them in order with ToonRenderer)
- Order: (line target of the screen-space outline) → stage beforeOpaque → opaque bodies → afterOpaque → outline shells of opaque things → screen-space outline → afterOutline
  → transparent things (farthest from the camera first, depth not written) → afterTransparent.
  Outlines are drawn together after all bodies to switch programs less, and transparent things are blended last from the farthest so what is behind shows through.
- Opaque things (bodies, outline shells, shadow depth) are drawn sorted by material, model and base color texture. (Ties keep the order they were added, so state changes less, like the Unity SRP Batcher)
  The depth test (LEQUAL) keeps the nearest one, so the screen is the same as in the added order. Only faces at exactly the same depth (overlapping planes) show the order, because the one drawn later wins.
  Merge such things into one model or offset their depth. Transparent things are drawn as before, farthest first in the added order.
- Transparent things: those whose alpha or tintColor alpha at draw time is below 1, or whose blendMode is not alpha. Their outline shells are drawn with them too (hasOutline).
- Groups: transparent things with the same options.group are sorted as one lump by the middle depth (average of the members) and drawn in the order they were added.
  If even one member of a group has options.isDepthPrepassed, that lump draws depth first and then paints color only on pixels with the same depth (LEQUAL).
  A hologram made of several overlapping parts shows through as one lump instead of being doubly bright. Lumps are drawn farthest first so they show through each other.
- Screen-space outline: if setScreenOutline(ToonScreenOutline) is given, draw draws opaque things into the line target before the bodies and blends it after the outline shells.
  The ID is options.lineId (the order added + 1 if not given, for instances instances[i].lineId comes first), and per model options.hasScreenOutline and options.hasCreaseLine turn it off and on.
  Transparent things are not drawn into the line target. If there is a screen rectangle (ToonRenderer.setScreenRect), that rectangle is used as the drawing area of the line target.
- Stage callbacks: callback(renderer, webGL2RenderingContext) of addPass(stage, callback) is called at that point. After the call, the renderer sets the frame's draw state again.
- Instance batches (addMeshInstanced) draw body and outline shell at once if opaque, and if transparent are sorted as one lump by the center of the instance positions.
- Shadows: drawShadows(renderer, shadowMap) draws only opaque things whose castsShadow is not false into the sun's shadow depth. Call it before draw.
  For point light and spotlight shadows, drawLocalShadows(renderer, shadowAtlas) draws the same things per atlas tile. (Set on the renderer with setLocalShadows)
- Use: every frame clear() → addMesh / addMeshInstanced / addPass → (drawShadows) → draw(renderer, camera) or drawWithMatrices(renderer, view matrix, projection matrix)
  draw calls renderer.beginFrameWithCamera(camera) and endFrame by itself. drawWithMatrices calls beginFrameWithMatrices. (Orthographic or raw matrix camera)
  The screen rectangle (ToonRenderer.setScreenRect) is set before that. clear empties all added models and stage callbacks. (The screen-space outline is kept)
- What is added are references to matrices and options. Do not change them until draw is called.

Owns the shared AudioContext and creates AudioPlayer instances.

Handling the browser autoplay policy:
 - Creating an AudioContext before the first user gesture (click/touch/keydown) makes the browser print a console warning ("AudioContext was not allowed to start ...").
 - So the AudioContext is created lazily, only after a user gesture has happened.
 - resumeContext() also silently does nothing before a user gesture.
 - For the case where createAudioPlayer() is called before a user gesture, the AudioContext is created (reluctantly) when the player is created, and only then a warning may appear.

Handling iOS updates (2026-10-22 03:41, confirmed on iOS 26.6.2):
 - On iOS, when a context restored by resumeContext() is "running", verifyContextClock() checks that the clock is really advancing.

Toon draw queue. (Holds the models to draw in a frame, then draws them in order with ToonRenderer)
- Order: (line target of the screen-space outline) → stage beforeOpaque → opaque bodies → afterOpaque → outline shells of opaque things → screen-space outline → afterOutline
  → transparent things (farthest from the camera first, depth not written) → afterTransparent.
  Outlines are drawn together after all bodies to switch programs less, and transparent things are blended last from the farthest so what is behind shows through.
- Opaque things (bodies, outline shells, shadow depth) are drawn sorted by material, model and base color texture. (Ties keep the order they were added, so state changes less, like the Unity SRP Batcher)
  The depth test (LEQUAL) keeps the nearest one, so the screen is the same as in the added order. Only faces at exactly the same depth (overlapping planes) show the order, because the one drawn later wins.
  Merge such things into one model or offset their depth. Transparent things are drawn as before, farthest first in the added order.
- Transparent things: those whose alpha or tintColor alpha at draw time is below 1, or whose blendMode is not alpha. Their outline shells are drawn with them too (hasOutline).
- Groups: transparent things with the same options.group are sorted as one lump by the middle depth (average of the members) and drawn in the order they were added.
  If even one member of a group has options.isDepthPrepassed, that lump draws depth first and then paints color only on pixels with the same depth (LEQUAL).
  A hologram made of several overlapping parts shows through as one lump instead of being doubly bright. Lumps are drawn farthest first so they show through each other.
- Screen-space outline: if setScreenOutline(ToonScreenOutline) is given, draw draws opaque things into the line target before the bodies and blends it after the outline shells.
  The ID is options.lineId (the order added + 1 if not given, for instances instances[i].lineId and for instance buffers the layout's instanceLineId slot comes first), and per model options.hasScreenOutline and options.hasCreaseLine turn it off and on.
  Transparent things are not drawn into the line target. If there is a screen rectangle (ToonRenderer.setScreenRect), that rectangle is used as the drawing area of the line target.
- Stage callbacks: callback(renderer, webGL2RenderingContext) of addPass(stage, callback) is called at that point. After the call, the renderer sets the frame's draw state again.
- Instance batches (addMeshInstanced) draw body and outline shell at once if opaque, and if transparent are sorted as one lump by the center of the instance positions.
  They are culled per instance and uploaded each time they are drawn. (The body, shadows and line target each upload the same array) Long-lived ones share a buffer uploaded once with addMeshInstanceBuffer.
- Instance buffers (addMeshInstanceBuffer) follow the form of Unity's Graphics.RenderMeshInstanced with GraphicsBuffer and Godot's MultiMesh. They are culled as a whole by the bounds of the entire buffer and not uploaded again.
- Shadows: drawShadows(renderer, shadowMap) draws only opaque things whose castsShadow is not false into the sun's shadow depth. Call it before draw.
  It follows setUpdateMode(ShadowUpdateMode) of the shadow target. The default onChange does not redraw when the lights and casters are unchanged, bakes the ones that stay still and draws only the moving ones on top. (The screen is the same as drawing every frame)
  For point light and spotlight shadows, drawLocalShadows(renderer, shadowAtlas) draws the same things per atlas tile. (Set on the renderer with setLocalShadows)
- Use: every frame clear() → addMesh / addMeshInstanced / addMeshInstanceBuffer / addPass → (drawShadows) → draw(renderer, camera) or drawWithMatrices(renderer, view matrix, projection matrix)
  draw calls renderer.beginFrameWithCamera(camera) and endFrame by itself. drawWithMatrices calls beginFrameWithMatrices. (Orthographic or raw matrix camera)
  The screen rectangle (ToonRenderer.setScreenRect) is set before that. clear empties all added models and stage callbacks. (The screen-space outline is kept)
- What is added are references to matrices and options. Do not change them until draw is called.

- When the texture slots fill up, when the blend, a stencil clip or a swapped-in shader changes, or when the buffer is full, what has accumulated is drawn, and the engine draws the rest at the end of the frame.
- Drawing outside the engine loop (a Graphic made without an engine, your own requestAnimationFrame, an input handler) is also drawn when that task ends (a microtask). That is before the browser presents the canvas, so it shows without an explicit flush, like a 2D canvas.
- When inserting a pass that touches WebGL directly (an external renderer and the like) while it is on, call flushBatch() first.

소리. (배경음악과 효과음)\n\n엔진의 AudioManager(공유 A:
Sound. (background music and sound effects)

Uses the engine's AudioManager (shared AudioContext) and AudioAsset (MP3). Plays downloaded sound buffers with Web Audio. (does not synthesize sound, only plays files)
Takes a sound table. Each row is { id, path or paths, volume, minimumInterval, isMusic, maximumVoices, pitchVariation, playSeconds, fadeOutSeconds }.
  volume: per-sound volume. (0 ~ 1, 1 if absent)  minimumInterval: interval before the same sound can play again. (seconds, so they do not pile up and get noisy)
  paths: a group of multiple recordings of the same sound. Picks one each time it plays, never the same as the one just before. (path if only one)
  maximumVoices: number of instances of the same sound that can play at once. (beyond that the oldest is cut off, if absent up to the total number of sound effects)
  pitchVariation: ratio by which the pitch varies on each play. (0.05 means ±5%, 0 if absent)
  playSeconds, fadeOutSeconds: plays only the first playSeconds seconds of a sound effect and fades it out over fadeOutSeconds seconds. (long files, to the end if absent or 0)
  loadType: load type. (AudioLoadType, background music uses streaming and sound effects use decompressOnLoad if absent, sound effects overlap so they must be fully decompressed to play)

Volume: background music = music volume setting × music ratio (half volume for the pause window, etc.) × sound volume, sound effect = sound effect volume setting × sound volume × volume at call time (attenuation by distance, etc.).
Background music can be crossfaded (fadeSeconds), and the stopped position is remembered per sound so it can resume from there. (isResumed)
Mute takes precedence over the volume setting. If any one of the following applies, no sound plays regardless of the settings.
  - Platform mute. (the function given with setExternalMuteProvider, the platform SDK's mute setting, while a rewarded ad is shown, etc.)
  - The user's mute button. (setUserMuted)
  - Page hidden. (another tab, app switch)
  - The window loses focus on a touch-primary device. (blur, when the app starts going to the background)
    On iPhone the page-hidden notification arrives after the app has gone to the background, by which time audio freezes without stopping and the last sound chunk repeats.
    The window focus-loss notification arrives before that. On desktop, clicking outside the canvas (the outer page) also loses focus, so it is not followed there.
Platform mute is read every frame (update), and page hiding is applied at that moment. (frames stop when hidden)
While muted, the AudioContext is also stopped. (suspend, resume when unmuted) On iPhone, if an app switch or interstitial ad takes over a running AudioContext,
no sound plays even when it is woken on return. If it is stopped on its own beforehand, sound plays again on return.
If the AudioContext is still not running after unmuting, it tries to wake it at short intervals until it runs. (iPhone sometimes ignores the wake at the moment of returning to the app)

If allowed (setAutoplayAllowedProvider, allowed if not given), it tries to wake once even before a press. If blocked, it turns on at the first press as below.
Browsers do not allow sound before the person first presses. Since the engine creates and wakes the AudioContext on the first press,
the sound paths (music and sound effect buses, AudioBus) are created after that, and sound plays only while the AudioContext is running. (so sounds requested while stopped do not all play at once on wake)
Buses are retrieved with getMusicBus and getEffectBus. Players made from a bus (AudioBus.createAudioPlayer) also follow the volume setting and mute.
The volume setting is applied directly to the bus's GainNode. So values set with the bus's setVolume and mute last only until SoundSystem applies the volume again.
Sound files are downloaded in the background so they do not block play. Sounds not yet downloaded or that failed to download simply do not play.

3D camera shake. (an engine shake in the form of Unity Cinemachine Impulse and Unreal Camera Shake)
- add(options) adds one shake. Each shake holds its own signal for 3 position axes and 3 rotation axes (pitch, yaw, roll), strength, frequency, duration, attack and decay.
- Signal: each axis layers two sine waves with slightly different frequencies. Phases and frequency ratios are drawn from the shake's seed. (same seed and same age give the same value)
- Envelope: 0 while age is negative (starts that much later), rises from 0 to 1 over attack seconds, decays as (1 - age / duration) to the power decayExponent and reaches 0 at duration.
- Stacking: all live shakes are summed. (unlike the 2D Shaker, which follows the stronger one)
- Age: options.age is the seconds already elapsed. The signal is also computed from age, so an event seen late and added with that age continues with the same values as if it had been added from the start.
- update(seconds) advances ages and removes finished shakes. read() gives the current offset { position, rotation }. (camera local axes)
- Where to apply: pass it to Camera3D.setViewOffset(position, rotation), or apply it with createOffsetViewMatrix to a view matrix the game computed.
- Seed: a shake added without options.seed draws its seed in turn from this object's seed (the seed given at construction).

툰 화면 공간 바깥선. (노멀, 선 번호, 깊이를 선의 판에 그리고, 바:
Toon screen-space outline. (Draws normals, line IDs and depth into the line target, picks lines at the boundaries between direct neighbors, widens them with jump flooding, then computes coverage from distance and blends)
- Line target: draws the result of ToonRenderer's createMesh once more with the same matrices and writes the normal (octahedral encoding), line ID (14 bits), flags (whether the silhouette line and crease line are on) and depth.
- Picking: each boundary between a pixel and its four direct neighbors is looked at once. A line stands not on a pixel but in the middle of the boundary between pixels. (The same boundary is not drawn twice)
  A silhouette line is where it touches empty space (the silhouette), where it touches a different ID, or where, even with the same ID, the two are farther apart than the depth threshold from each other's tangent plane (occluded silhouette).
  A crease line is where two neighboring normals within the same ID open wider than the crease angle. Since only normals one pixel apart are compared, no band appears around the silhouette of round surfaces or on slanted surfaces.
  Depth is compared as tangent plane distance, so no false lines appear on a floor seen at a grazing angle. Twice the pixel size at that depth is added to the threshold so distant things mean the same.
- Widening: the distance to the boundary segments is spread with jump flooding. The step count is log2 regardless of thickness, and silhouette and crease lines are spread separately to give separate thicknesses.
- Blending: each pixel of the drawing area is covered by clamp(thickness / 2 - distance + 0.5, 0, 1) from the distance to the nearest boundary. (Soft edges, and no stairs or dotted lines even when the widening target is reduced)
- Per model: if hasScreenOutline of drawMesh is false, that model produces no line and only hides lines behind it. If hasCreaseLine is false, only crease lines are turned off.
- Per-ID color: setLineColor gives a line color per ID. (The Unreal Custom Stencil form; a line where two IDs touch takes the color of the nearer ID, and IDs not in the table, or an empty table, keep the setColor color)
- Thickness: the thickness of setWidth and setCrease is the thickness of one line. (Half on each side of the boundary) The unit is ToonOutlineWidthUnit, and it does not go below one pixel.
- Depth: orthographic and perspective are told apart by the projection matrix, and depth is unpacked into view-space position for comparison. (Projections whose clip x and y were moved, like a screen rectangle, also work)
- Cost: setResolutionScale reduces the widening (jump flooding) target. (The light path for phones) The line target and seeds stay at drawing area resolution, so line positions do not change when reduced.
- Instances: drawMeshInstanced culls the instance array and uploads it then. drawMeshInstanceBuffer shares the ToonRenderer.createInstanceBuffer buffer with the body and does not upload it again.
  The ID of each instance in the buffer is read from the layout's instanceLineId slot. (The common ID if there is none)
- Use: every frame beginLineIds(view, projection) → drawMesh / drawMeshInstanced / drawMeshInstanceBuffer → endLineIds() (computes seeds and widening) → draw the toon bodies → drawOutline().
  beginLineIds notes the current viewport as the drawing area and builds the line target to fit its size. endLineIds and drawOutline restore the framebuffer, viewport and state.
  If handed over with ToonDrawQueue.setScreenOutline, the draw queue does this sequence by itself. (When inserted between engine 2D drawing, call Graphic.flushBatch before it)

Toon material. (Shader chunks inserted into ToonRenderer's body shader, the per-game extension point)
- Only patterns and effects that the engine's standard features (textures, light, tint, blending) cannot do go into chunks. Slots without a chunk get the engine's empty functions.
- uniformChunk: goes into the top slot of the fragment shader. Write uniforms, constants, functions and the ins exported by the vertex chunk.
- surfaceChunk: defines void applySurface(inout ToonSurface surface). The engine calls it after computing the vertex color, textures and decal, before tint and light.
  ToonSurface { vec3 baseColor (sRGB), float alpha, vec3 emission (linear), vec3 normal (world, unit), float glow (vertex glow), bool isUnlit,
                vec4 detail (vertex pattern number and pattern color), vec2 uv, vec2 uv1 (second UV, (0, 1) if none), vec3 localPosition (model coordinates), vec3 worldPosition, vec3 viewDirection (from the surface toward the camera, unit),
                float shadeOffset (value added to the received light amount, moves the shade boundary), float specularMask (highlight multiplier), float rimMask (rim light multiplier) }
- lightChunk: defines void applyLight(ToonSurface surface, inout ToonLighting lighting). The engine calls it after gathering the sun, ambient light, fill, point lights and spotlights, highlight and rim, before combining.

Reads models painted with material colors. Texture coordinates and material textures are read too if present.
  - One part is one node, and a node's mesh is one primitive per color. Vertices are position and normal, plus joint indices and weights if there is a skeleton.
    A primitive without normals is read with flat normals (one per triangle) as the glTF 2.0 specification says. Vertices are split per triangle and given the face normal. (The same goes for the rebuilt outline shell)
  - The material's baseColorFactor is a linear color, so it is converted to sRGB, and emissiveFactor, if present, is stored as glow. (If there is an emissiveTexture, glow is passed only through the material range)
  - TEXCOORD_0, if present, goes into uvData and TEXCOORD_1 into uv1Data (second UV, angel ring). A material range (materialRanges) is stored per primitive.
    { name material name, materialIndex, nodeName, indexStart, indexCount, extras material extras, alphaMode, alphaCutoff, baseColorFactor linear, emissiveFactor linear, baseColorImage, emissiveImage (images order, -1 if none), hasUv }
    When painting split areas inside a part (accent color areas, display panels), pick them by material name or extras and draw only that area with indexStart and indexCount of ToonRenderer.drawMesh.
  - Images are read with readGlbImages, decoded with decodeGlbImage and passed to ToonRenderer.createTexture.
  - outline in material extras is an outline shell (only back faces drawn), and basic is a part that does not receive light.
    If outlineOptions is given, that shell is not stored, and a shell of uniform thickness per point is newly built from the body of each node that has a ".outline" pair. (MeshBuilder.addTriangleShell)
  - If there is a skeleton (skin), the joint nodes and their inverse bind matrices, the animations and their extras (hitAt of an attack, loop "once" that plays only once, and so on) are read together. Poses are computed by writeSkinPose.
  - Models whose parts are hidden or painted separately (like a cluster of several crystals) are read per node with readGlbNodeArrays.
    Node extras (pivot where doors and legs rotate, and so on) are stored as that part's extras.
  - For a skeletal model read as one lump (like a vehicle), node extras, part positions and the joints they follow are read separately with readGlbNodeInfos.
  - GLB files whose vertex attributes are stored as integers (KHR_mesh_quantization) are read too. Normalized integers are divided with the glTF spec formulas, and texture coordinates get the material texture KHR_texture_transform baked in.
    An unnamed mesh node belongs to the part of its named parent node. (the leaf node a quantizer adds for the dequantization transform) If extensionsRequired lists an extension that cannot be read (meshopt compression and others), an error is thrown.
The engine's GLB reader is tied inside the engine's PBR model (SkinnedModel), so only the vertex arrays used for toon drawing are extracted here.

선 번호 어트리뷰트의 자리. (사용자 어트리뷰트의 마지막 자리, 선의 판: Location of the line ID attribute. (The last user attribute location, the line target shader reads from this location)
툰 HDR 마무리. (실수 렌더 타겟에 그린 선형 색을 블룸, 노출, 톤:
Toon HDR finishing. (outputs linear color drawn to a float render target to the screen with bloom, exposure, tone mapping and gamma)
- Combines RenderTarget (half-float color, depth), BloomEffect (or MultiLevelBloomEffect) and FullscreenPass.
- Usage: after ToonRenderer.setHdrOutput(true), begin(background linear color) → draw with ToonRenderer → end(output framebuffer, viewport)
  end (resolves first if multisampled) computes bloom and draws the tone-mapped color into the output framebuffer (screen if null).
- Constructor options: new ToonPostProcess(gl, width, height, { sampleCount, useFloatColor, depthBits, useDepthTexture }) (without options, same as now: RGBA16F, depth 16, no multisampling)
  If sampleCount is 2 or more, the scene is drawn to a multisampled (MSAA) renderbuffer and resolved to a texture before end. Reduced to a count the device supports. (getSampleCount, setSampleCount)
  depthBits 24 means 24-bit depth. (scenes with a distant far plane) useDepthTexture keeps the scene depth as a texture. (used by setLitArea)
- Color space: linear color is written to the scene render target. (ToonRenderer.setHdrOutput(true), ToonScreenOutline.setHdrOutput(true), ToonVfx colors are also treated as linear)
  Games that wrote gamma-encoded color g to the float target and converted back with g^2.2 in compositing should convert those values to linear beforehand. Colors become c^2.2, and a brightness multiplier k applied on the gamma side becomes linear k^2.2.
  (e.g. 1.37 is linear 2, 1.6 is 2.81, 2.08 is 5, brightness 1.6 with multiplier 1.6 gives (1.6 x 1.6)^2.2 = 7.9) Bloom threshold and knee are linear brightness.
  These examples hold only for a multiplier that was applied on the gamma side (to the gamma-encoded color g). A multiplier that was applied to linear colors, and values that are linear from the start such as the bloom threshold and knee, are passed as they are without conversion.
- Devices that cannot use float targets: even with useFloatColor (default true), if ToonPostProcess.isFloatColorSupported is false, RGBA8 targets are built. (getUseFloatColor is false)
  That case and useFloatColor: false take the LDR path. The scene is drawn in screen color (gamma-encoded color, ToonRenderer.setHdrOutput(false)), and compositing adds bloom without tone mapping and gamma and applies only color grading.
- Bloom: default is a half-resolution 9-tap Gaussian (BloomEffect, threshold 0.9 ~ 1.6, ping-pong targets RGBA8, RGBA16F with setBloomFloatColor).
  Giving setBloomLevels(level count, threshold, knee) a level count of 1 or more switches to MultiLevelBloomEffect (halves down then scales up with a tent filter while adding, targets at the same precision as the scene). 0 restores the default. Strength is applied to both by setBloom.
- Tone mapping is the ACES approximation (Krzysztof Narkowicz 2016, whose post lets it be used under CC0 or MIT). Exposure (setExposure) is multiplied in before mapping, then sRGB gamma is applied.
- Color grading: after gamma, applies in order brightness (setBrightness, toward 1 inside the lit area setLitArea), saturation, color tone (multiplies a color normalized to brightness 1), fog light (pulls dark areas toward that color), contrast, edge darkening. (setColorGrade, setVignette)
  Defaults are brightness 1, saturation 1, contrast 1, color tone 0, fog light 0, edge 0, so there is no grading.
- Resolution scale: with setResolutionScale(scale), the scene target is built at output size x scale and scaled up to end's viewport (linear filtering) for output. (to render only 3D at a lower resolution while leaving UI at device pixels, default 1)
- Outputting inside a node rectangle: resize(rectangle width, height) → begin → draw (leave ToonRenderer's screen rectangle cleared) → end(null, [x, drawing buffer height - y - height, width, height]).
하위 트리 그리기 경계 셈하기. (자기 그림과 켜지고 보이는 자식들 경계:
Calculates subtree draw bounds. (The union of the node's own drawing and its enabled, visible children's bounds; readSubtreeDrawBounds calls it only after a change; true if known)
- Own drawing: calculateDrawnRect and enabled components. Components drawing only inside the content area (Component.isDrawnInsideContent) count as the content area grown by one unit,
  components drawing outside use Component.calculateDrawnRect. Components that draw nothing (no draw override) are skipped;
  a single unknown component makes the bounds unknown. A node drawing gizmos, or one whose content size cannot be read (when it has inside-content components), is also unknown.
- Children: each child's subtree bounds moved by the child (transformDrawBoundsToParent) into this node's content coordinates. A child with unknown placement makes the bounds unknown.
- Even when unknown, all enabled and visible children's bounds are read. (Children must cache theirs so descendant changes propagate up to this node)
- Each child's bounds moved into parent coordinates are written onto the child. (readParentDrawBounds, which the draw traversal checks before applying the child's transform, valid until this node recalculates)
- Bounds are not shrunk by masks clipping children. (Kept generous)
경계를 적을 곳. (부모의 내용 좌표, 크기가 0 이면 아무것도 그리지: Where to write the bounds. (In the parent's content coordinates; a size of 0 means nothing is drawn)
맞는 경계가 있으면 참. (없으면 rect 를 건드리지 않는다): True if valid bounds exist. (Otherwise rect is left untouched)
부모가 셈해 둔 이 노드의 하위 트리 그리기 경계 읽기. (부모의 내용:
Reads this node's subtree draw bounds as calculated by the parent. (In the parent's content coordinates, the bounding box with this node's transform applied; true if valid)
- The parent writes these for each child when it calculates its subtree bounds (calculateSubtreeDrawBounds). When this node's transform or bounds change the parent recalculates, so they are reused until then.
- The draw traversal checks this rectangle first under the parent's transform and skips this node without applying its transform when it lies outside the visible rectangle in parent coordinates. (Scrolling changes only the parent's transform, so children are not recalculated one by one)
- False if the parent has not calculated yet or something changed since (a recalculation is due), or if where this node draws or where it is placed is unknown.
부모가 셈해 둔 줄의 경계를 부모 좌표로 읽기: Reading a row's bounds calculated by its parent, in parent coordinates
그리는 사각형 셈하기. (오버라이드: 살아 있는 파티클이 그리는 쿼드를:
Calculates the drawn rectangle. (Override: a rectangle enclosing every quad the live particles draw, in node content coordinates)
- Each particle grows by half its drawn size times √2 (rotated rectangles, images), streak quads enclose head and tail grown by half the width, the wobble amplitude is added left and right, plus one unit of margin.
- Recalculation is requested whenever the simulation (simulate) runs, on emit and on clearing (stop), and in setters that change how particles are drawn. (Drawing is skipped when off screen while the simulation keeps running in tick)
- With no particles the size is 0 (nothing is drawn).
- Unknown when in world space with manual tick. (Moving the node moves where it draws and there is no point at which to recalculate)
그리는 사각형 셈하기. (오버라이드: 점을 이은 띠를 모두 품는 사각형,:
Calculates the drawn rectangle. (Override: a rectangle enclosing the band joining the points, in node content coordinates)
- Points are drawn relative to the node position, so they are moved by the current node position and grown by half the larger of the two widths plus one unit of margin. (Covering line ends and joins)
- Recalculation is requested every tick while points exist, on clear, and when the width changes. With fewer than two points nothing is drawn, so the size is 0.
지나간 자리를 품는 사각형: A rectangle enclosing the path travelled
경계 상자를 적을 곳. (지금 변환의 지역 좌표): Where to write the bounding box. (In the current transform's local coordinates)
알면 참. (모르면 rect 를 건드리지 않는다): True if known. (Otherwise rect is left untouched)
보이는 사각형(화면과 걸린 자르기)을 지금 변환의 지역 좌표로 거꾸로 옮:
Reads the visible rectangle (the screen and active clips) moved back into the current transform's local coordinates as a bounding box. (Only while subtree culling is on; true if known)
- With rotation or skew it is conservative (the bounding box of the four corners, grown by one device pixel). Anything drawn outside this rectangle is not visible.
- Used by a node to find the visible range among many children (TransformNode.drawChildren). Not recalculated while the transform and clip stay the same.
- False if off-screen culling or subtree culling is off, all gizmos are drawn, the viewport is not set yet, or the transform cannot be inverted (scale 0).
지금 변환에서 보이는 사각형 읽기: Reading the visible rectangle under the current transform
The number of subtrees to add.
Adds to the number of subtrees whose drawing was skipped entirely this frame because they were off screen. (TransformNode.drawChildren calls it after skipping the children outside the visible range at once)
자식 목록 출력. (자식 차례대로 Graphic.drawNode, dra:
Draws the children. (Graphic.drawNode for each child in order; called by draw)
- While subtree culling is on, the visible range of children is narrowed by binary search against the visible rectangle in parent coordinates (Graphic.readLocalVisibleBounds), and the children before and after it are not called.
  The range is found from the children's bounds written when the subtree bounds were calculated (the largest bottom and right gathered from the front, the smallest top and left gathered from the back), so it is correct in any child order,
  and when children are laid out in order like rows only the visible rows remain. A child with unknown bounds stops the narrowing past it. Drawing order is unchanged.
- If this node's bounds change while drawing (such as a child moving a sibling), all remaining children are called.
